workflow.remark: Two corrections from the researcher. (1) The NASA Exoplanet Archive column is tran_flag, not tr_flag; tr_flag does not exist in pscomppars or ps, so the declared loads would fail. Use tran_flag in both tables. (2) Radius provenance: the archive itself labels radii it calculated from mass. In pscomppars, pl_rade_reflink contains refstr=CALCULATED_VALUE (link text 'Calculated Value', documented at https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html, mass-radius relation of Chen and Kipping 2017) for these radii. A probe on 2026-10-13 found 1,537 such rows, all with tran_flag = 0, out of 1,634 planets with tran_flag = 0. Make the primary rule: calculated = pl_rade_reflink contains CALCULATED_VALUE; measured otherwise. Cross-tabulate it against tran_flag and discoverymethod, and report the non-transiting planets whose radius is not marked calculated (about 97: imaging, timing and other methods) as their own group, not as measured-from-transit. Load pl_radelim and pl_orbperlim as well. Drop the reference-by-reference hand coding and the 50-planet manual validation: they cannot be done or checked in this run. Keep the ps default-solution table only if it can be classified with the same rule; otherwise leave it out and say so.

workflow.text: Researcher decisions at the design review: the radius-provenance rule in data_dictionary.json (the archive's CALCULATED_VALUE label in pl_rade_reflink; groups calculated, measured_transiting, measured_non_transiting, no_radius) replaces Section 4 of paper_plan.md. There is no reference-level hand coding, no 50-planet manual validation and no ps default-solution robustness table. pl_controv_flag is not loaded, so controversial planets are not excluded; say so in the sample description. Main comparison: calculated versus measured_transiting; report measured_non_transiting separately and never describe it as measured from a transit. Keep the paper short: the main tables, figures 1 to 4 and the mass-radius diagnostic for the calculated group.

workflow.remark: One substantive error in the conclusion. It says the pattern of two radius humps 'belongs mostly to the 80 percent of the sample with transit-measured radii'. That holds for the hump at 2 to 4 Earth radii (1,901 of 2,090) but not for the hump at 8 to 15 Earth radii: 846 of its 1,529 planets have calculated radii, more than half. So the giant-planet hump of the pooled diagram is largely made of radii the archive calculated from mass. State this in the results (where the two humps are described), in the abstract and in the conclusion, using the counts already in the results (846 of 1,529; 1,901 of 2,090). Do not add any other claims. Keep everything else as it is.
